holidays.name: Checkers Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the classic board game of checkers, and also the most famous dog in American political history. Dust off the board, challenge a friend to a few jumps, and crown some kings.
holidays.origin: The date marks Richard Nixon's televised 'Checkers speech' on September 23, 1952. In it, he defended his campaign finances and said he would keep one gift, a cocker spaniel named Checkers.
holidays.funFact: Checkers is among the oldest games still played. Ancestors of the game date back thousands of years, and in Britain it is called draughts.

holidays.name: National Dogs in Politics Day
holidays.description: A tail-wagging salute to the political pups who have padded through the halls of power. Think presidential pets, campaign mascots and the occasional four-legged scandal.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance tied to the same date as Nixon's 1952 Checkers speech. That speech is the best-known moment when a dog took center stage in a political campaign.
holidays.funFact: The Checkers speech drew an enormous TV audience, and Nixon stayed on the ticket. Checkers the dog became a household name.
